description: Examine the genetic and environmental foundations of cognitive ability, analyzing twin studies, the Flynn effect, environmental enrichment, intellectual disability, and giftedness.

slides.title: The Nature vs. Nurture Question in Intellect
slides.content:
# The Great Intelligence Debate: Genes and Environment

Is human intellectual capability pre-programmed in our DNA at conception, or is it sculpted by the richness of our childhood environment, nutrition, and schooling?

## Beyond False Dichotomies:
Modern behavioral genetics rejects simplistic either/or thinking. Intelligence is the complex, dynamic product of **Gene-Environment Interaction (G x E)**:

```
                             [THE NATURE-NURTURE INTERFACE]
                                            |
         +----------------------------------+----------------------------------+
         |                                                                     |
   [GENETIC ARCHITECTURE]                                        [ENVIRONMENTAL ARCHITECTURE]
   - Polygenic Inheritance & GWAS                                - The Flynn Effect (Secular IQ Rise)
   - Twin and Adoption Studies (MISTRA)                          - Environmental Enrichment (Abecedarian Project)
   - The Wilson Effect (Heritability increases with age!)        - Biological Hazards: Toxins & Toxic Stress
```

slides.title: Heritability Defined: What It Is and Isn't
slides.content:
# Demystifying Heritability: What Does h-squared Mean?

In behavioral genetics, **Heritability (h^2)** is one of the most frequently misunderstood statistical concepts in science:

```
   HERITABILITY DEFINITION:
   The proportion of TOTAL PHENOTYPIC VARIATION in a trait within a SPECIFIC POPULATION
   that is attributable to GENETIC VARIATION among individuals.
```

## Critical Misconceptions Dispelled:
- **Heritability applies to POPULATIONS, NEVER to an individual!** (You cannot say *"50% of your personal intelligence came from genes"*).
- **Heritability is NOT fixed!** If the environment changes dramatically (e.g., universal equal schooling for all), heritability surges toward 100% because all remaining differences are genetic!
- Meta-analyses across hundreds of twin studies estimate the heritability of intelligence between **50% and 80% in adulthood**.

slides.title: The Wilson Effect: Increasing Heritability with Age
slides.content:
# Ronald Wilson: The Genetic Surge (1983)

Common sense would assume that as humans grow older and accumulate decades of environmental schooling, the influence of genetics on intelligence should decrease. **The exact opposite occurs!**

## The Wilson Effect:
The heritability of intelligence **STEADILY INCREASES ACROSS THE LIFESPAN**:

```
   DEVELOPMENTAL STAGE         HERITABILITY ESTIMATE (h^2)
   ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Infancy (~ 1 year old)   --> h^2 = approx 0.20 (20%)
   Childhood (~ 8 years old)--> h^2 = approx 0.40 (40%)
   Adolescence (~ 16 years) --> h^2 = approx 0.60 (60%)
   Mature Adulthood         --> h^2 = approx 0.70 to 0.80 (70% - 80%!)

slides.title: Why Does Heritability Increase with Age?
slides.content:
# Active Gene-Environment Correlation: Sandra Scarr

Why does genetics dominate in adulthood? Sandra Scarr and Kathleen McCartney explained this via **Gene-Environment Correlations (rGE)**:

```
   1. PASSIVE rGE (Infancy):    Parents provide both genes and environment. (Child has zero control).
   2. EVOCATIVE rGE (Childhood):Child's genetic curiosity evokes positive reactions from teachers.
   3. ACTIVE rGE (Adulthood):   Adults gain total AUTONOMY to actively SELECT and SHAPE their own
                                intellectual niches (choosing college, reading books, selecting careers)!
```

Individuals genetically predisposed to high curiosity seek out intellectually stimulating environments (**Niche Picking**), compounding genetic advantages across adulthood!

slides.title: Heritability & Wilson Effect Check
slides.content: Verify your understanding of heritability definitions and age trends!
slides.quizQuestion: In behavioral genetics, what is the 'Wilson Effect' regarding the heritability of human intelligence across development?
quizOptions: The heritability of intelligence drops to zero by age 10
The heritability of intelligence systematically increases as an individual ages from infancy (~20%) to mature adulthood (~70-80%) due to active niche-picking
Genetics only matters for musical ability

slides.title: Twin & Adoption Studies: The Minnesota Study (MISTRA)
slides.content:
# Thomas Bouchard: Separated at Birth

Thomas Bouchard and colleagues at the University of Minnesota tracked over 100 pairs of **Identical Twins Reared Apart (MZA)** from birth:

```
   TWIN RELATIONSHIP                           IQ CORRELATION (r)
   ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Identical Twins Reared Together (MZT)   --> r = 0.86 (Nearly identical!)
   Identical Twins Reared Apart (MZA)      --> r = 0.76 (Astonishingly close!)
   Fraternal Twins Reared Together (DZT)   --> r = 0.60
   Biological Siblings Reared Together     --> r = 0.47
   Adoptive Siblings (Unrelated)           --> r = 0.30 in childhood (DROPS TO 0.00 IN ADULTHOOD!)
```

MZA twins who never met until age 40 shared identical mannerisms, voice tones, intellectual test scores, and even identical quirky habits!

slides.title: James Flynn & The Flynn Effect: The Environmental Proof
slides.content:
# James Flynn: The Secular Rise in Global IQ

In 1984, political scientist **James Flynn** documented a shocking global phenomenon: Raw scores on standardized IQ tests have been **rising by approx 3 IQ points per decade (approx 30 points per century!)** across all industrialized nations!

```
   RAW IQ TEST PERFORMANCE ACROSS THE 20th CENTURY:
   An average person in 1920 scoring 100 on today's test norms would have an IQ of only 70!
   An average person today scoring 100 on 1920 test norms would have an IQ of 130 (Gifted)!
```

## Why Human Genetics Did NOT Change in 80 Years:
Human gene pools cannot evolve in three generations! The Flynn Effect proves the immense power of **Environmental Modernization**: universal formal education, improved childhood nutrition, infectious disease eradication, and exposure to rich digital visual complexity.

slides.title: Environmental Enrichment: The Abecedarian Project
slides.content:
# Proving Plasticity: Early Intervention

Can intensive environmental intervention permanently raise cognitive functioning in disadvantaged children?

## The Carolina Abecedarian Project (Campbell & Ramey):
- Infants from low-income, high-risk families were randomly assigned to high-quality full-time cognitive and linguistic enrichment (starting at infancy, 5 days/week for 5 years):

```
   LONGITUDINAL ADULT OUTCOMES TRACKED TO AGE 30+:
   - Maintained significant, enduring IQ ADVANTAGES over control peers for decades!
   - FOUR TIMES MORE LIKELY TO GRADUATE FROM A 4-YEAR UNIVERSITY (23% vs. 6%)!
   - Significantly higher income, superior health markers, and drastically lower incarceration!
```

slides.content: Verify your understanding of secular IQ trends and early intervention!

quizOptions: It proves that human genetic DNA mutated completely in two generations

slides.title: Biological & Environmental Hazards to Intellect
slides.content:
# Cognitive Toxins: Destroying Neural Potential

While good environments boost intelligence, biological hazards inflict severe, permanent cognitive damage:

## 1. Neurotoxic Lead (Pb) Exposure (Needleman, 1979):
- Even microscopic levels of lead in blood disrupt neurotransmitter release and synaptogenesis, causing irreversible drops of **4 to 7 IQ points**, attention deficits, and elevated violent crime.

## 2. Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorders (FASD):
- Alcohol crosses the placenta, destroying migrating fetal neural crest cells; leading preventable non-genetic cause of intellectual disability.

## 3. Severe Iodine Deficiency:
- Eradicated in nations via iodized salt; untreated iodine deficiency causes congenital hypothyroidism (cretinism), dropping population IQ by **10 to 15 points**!

slides.title: Intellectual Disability: Diagnostic Dimensions
slides.content:
# DSM-5 Criteria: Intellectual Disability (ID)

The DSM-5 abandoned the old term "mental retardation" and established three mandatory diagnostic prongs for **Intellectual Disability**:

```
   1. DEFICITS IN INTELLECTUAL FUNCTIONING:
      - Confirmed by clinical assessment and standardized testing (IQ <= 70 +- 5 for SEM).
   
   2. DEFICITS IN ADAPTIVE FUNCTIONING (Fails to meet developmental and sociocultural standards):
      - Conceptual Domain: Language, reading, writing, math, reasoning, memory.
      - Social Domain: Interpersonal empathy, friendship abilities, social judgment.
      - Practical Domain: Personal care, job responsibilities, money management, safety.
   
   3. ONSET DURING THE DEVELOPMENTAL PERIOD (Prior to age 18).
```

*Severity Level (Mild, Moderate, Severe, Profound)* is determined by **Adaptive Functioning**, NOT by IQ score alone!

slides.title: Genetic Etiologies of Intellectual Disability
slides.content:
# Biological Causes: Chromosomal and Metabolic Syndromes

Over 300 genetic conditions cause intellectual disability:

```
   CONDITION                     CHROMOSOMAL / GENETIC MECHANISM             PHENOTYPIC MANIFESTATION
   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   1. Down Syndrome           --> Trisomy 21 (An extra copy of chromosome 21)--> Mild to moderate ID, epicanthic
                                  due to non-disjunction during meiosis.      folds, early Alzheimer's risk.
   2. Fragile X Syndrome      --> CGG trinucleotide repeat expansion on      --> Most common inherited cause of ID;
                                  FMR1 gene on the X chromosome.              large ears, autistic features.
   3. Phenylketonuria (PKU)   --> Inability to synthesize phenylalanine      --> Toxic buildup causes severe ID;
                                  hydroxylase (autosomal recessive).          **100% PREVENTED VIA DIET!**
```

slides.content: Verify your understanding of DSM-5 diagnostic criteria and genetic etiologies!
slides.quizQuestion: In the DSM-5, how is the clinical severity level (Mild, Moderate, Severe, or Profound) of Intellectual Disability officially determined?
quizOptions: Exclusively by the exact numerical IQ score on a WAIS test
By the individual's level of adaptive functioning across conceptual, social, and practical life domains

By counting the number of letters in the patient's name

slides.title: Intellectual Giftedness: Lewis Terman's Termites
slides.content:
# Lewis Terman: The Myth of the Mad Genius (1921)

Historically, popular folklore viewed intellectually gifted children as physically weak, socially awkward, and mentally unstable. In 1921, Lewis Terman launched the longest longitudinal study in history, tracking **1,528 California children with IQs > 135 ("The Termites")** for 60 years:

## Terman's Groundbreaking Findings:
- Gifted children were **taller, physically stronger, healthier, and socially well-adjusted**!
- As adults, they earned significantly more graduate degrees, produced thousands of patents and books, earned higher incomes, and had lower rates of divorce and alcoholism.
- *Key Exception:* Terman's study over-represented affluent families and missed two Nobel laureates (William Shockley and Luis Alvarez) who tested just below the 135 cutoff!

slides.title: Richard Gottesman's Reaction Range Model
slides.content:
# Unifying Nature and Nurture: The Reaction Range

Behavioral geneticist Richard Gottesman synthesized genes and environment into **The Reaction Range Model**:

```
   GENES SET THE BOUNDARIES:       Genetics establishes an upper and lower biological potential range
                                  (e.g., a Reaction Range of 20 to 25 IQ points).
                                                |
                                                v
   ENVIRONMENT SETS THE PLACEMENT: Environment determines EXACTLY WHERE within that genetic
                                  range an individual will actually fall!
```

```
   Individual A (Genetically endowed with Reaction Range 100 - 125):
   - Reared in enriched, loving, well-nourished home --> ACHIEVES FULL POTENTIAL: IQ = 125!
   - Reared in deprived, lead-poisoned, abusive home --> STUNTED AT BOTTOM: IQ = 100!
```

slides.title: Epigenetics: How Environment Regulates DNA
slides.content:
# The Molecular Bridge: Epigenetics

Epigenetics proves that the environment can physically alter **gene expression without changing the underlying DNA code**:

- **DNA Methylation & Histone Modification:** Environmental stressors (chronic childhood abuse, maternal starvation) attach chemical methyl groups to DNA molecules, switching cognitive genes permanently off!
- **Intergenerational Transmission:** Traumatic stress can alter germline epigenetic tags, transmitting stress vulnerability to future offspring.

slides.content: Verify your understanding of Terman's giftedness research and the reaction range!
slides.quizQuestion: In Richard Gottesman's Reaction Range Model of intelligence, what roles do genetics and environment play in determining an individual's final cognitive phenotype?
quizOptions: Genetics determines 100% of intelligence; environment has zero effect

slides.title: Comprehensive Nature vs. Nurture Comparison Matrix
slides.content:
# Theoretical Architecture of Cognitive Variation

| Level of Analysis | Core Phenomenon | Key Scientific Finding |
|---|---|---|
| **Behavioral Genetics** | Twin Studies (MISTRA) | Identical twins reared apart share r = 0.76 IQ correlation. |
| **Lifespan Genetics** | The Wilson Effect | Heritability surges with age as active niche-picking takes over. |
| **Secular Environmental**| The Flynn Effect | IQ scores rose ~30 points in the 20th century due to modernization. |
| **Enrichment Trials** | Abecedarian Project | High-quality early childhood intervention permanently boosts life outcomes. |
| **Clinical Genetics** | Down & Fragile X Syndromes | Chromosomal non-disjunction & CGG repeats cause clinical ID. |
| **Interactionist Synthesis**| Gottesman's Reaction Range | Genetics sets potential boundaries; environment dictates final outcome. |

slides.title: Module Synthesis: Nature vs. Nurture in Intelligence
slides.content:

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                 MODULE SUMMARY MATRIX                                   |
+-----------------------+-----------------------------+-----------------------------------+
| Concept / Model       | Key Pioneers                | Core Scientific Principle         |
+-----------------------+-----------------------------+-----------------------------------+

|                       |                             | applies to population variance.   |
+-----------------------+-----------------------------+-----------------------------------+
| The Wilson Effect     | Ronald Wilson (1983)        | Heritability increases with age   |
|                       |                             | via active niche picking.         |
+-----------------------+-----------------------------+-----------------------------------+
| The Flynn Effect      | James Flynn (1984, 1987)    | Raw IQ rose ~3 pts/decade due to  |
|                       |                             | environmental modernization.      |
+-----------------------+-----------------------------+-----------------------------------+
| Reaction Range Model  | Richard Gottesman (1963)    | Genetics sets the boundaries;     |
|                       |                             | environment sets the placement.   |
+-----------------------+-----------------------------+-----------------------------------+
```

## Final Lesson:
Nature and nurture are not warring rivals; they are inseparable collaborative partners. Our genetic blueprint provides the raw potential, while our cultural, nutritional, and educational environments determine how brilliantly that potential blossoms.
